would_leave_at: around 8s, once the second round reveals the same format and I realize the video is mostly repeated countdowns
first_impression: Polished enough nutrition trivia, but it feels slow, repetitive, and slightly error-prone rather than sharp and shareable.
problems: The hook is only moderately strong; “More vitamin C?” is interesting, but the cover has no surprising claim or visual food cue to stop the scroll.
The video spends too much time on countdowns versus payoff; 19 seconds is long for three simple comparisons.
The repeated split-screen format makes the second and third questions predictable.
There are visible transition/export mistakes at 11s and 16s.
Small source text and tiny per-100g labels may be hard to read on mobile, especially with platform UI overlays.
Data inconsistencies between reveal frames make the post look less credible.
The final summary card is useful but visually quieter than the versus cards, so it ends flat.
The brand CTA in the caption does not naturally connect to the content, so it may feel like engagement bait leading into an unrelated product plug.
fixes: Cut the runtime to 9-12 seconds: show each question for about 1 second, then reveal immediately; remove or shorten the countdowns.
Make the first frame more surprising, e.g. “This has 2.4x more vitamin C than an orange” with the red pepper partially hidden, or “Orange loses?”
Fix all data values so they are consistent across question, reveal, and final summary cards.
Remove the transition glitches at 11s and 16s; check exported layers for stray text and mistimed round labels.
Vary the pacing or animation between rounds so it does not feel like the exact same template three times.
Increase legibility of the smallest labels and source text, or move source detail to the final card/caption only.
Make the final card more punchy: “Winners: red bell pepper, baked potato, ketchup” with one memorable takeaway.
If keeping the RecipeFix CTA, connect it more naturally in the caption, or omit it from this post and let the food fact stand on its own.
